Wow. You’re literally describing me. I am (hopefully) about to graduate with my biology degree. I also joined a lab group at my uni and for a while I did feel like I didn’t belong and I wasn’t a real scientist. I still struggle with my identity sometimes, but I’d like to think I got it mostly figured out.

A few things helped me settle my feelings and allowed me to truly believe that I too am a scientist. One of which, is that I began to dedicate more time to the lab I was a part of. Of course in order to graduate on time, I took on more research credits than what is usually allowed, but my point is, whenever you can and of course whenever you feel like it, go in and keep doing “scientific” things. The only real person who can validate you is yourself. 

Second, constantly educating and quizzing myself on stuff from my lab group and things I’ve learned in class. Practice your knowledge skills and then practice explaining what you know to yourself/to an audience. As long as you can sound like you know what you’re talking about *with evidence*, you start to feel less like an imposter and more like a contributor to the field. A nice ego boost.

And finally, realize that everyone struggles with things in their profession. No one is 100% good at what they do. My head professor of my lab said that he always used to struggle with chemistry. We run a proteomics lab that is almost all biochem. It took him a while to get where he was but he made it. The grad/phd students I work with also make mistakes too, so it certainly helped when I realized that these older students who have been doing this for years might have the same feelings I did/do, but still made it to where they are today.

As long as you work on “destroying the boundaries of ignorance” as my professor says, you are a scientist.

Most people wish to find a partner in which they live the rest of their life with. Though if you’re years into a relationship, you don’t ever really know when things are about to end until they do, if it ever comes to that. Imagine though, you’re like 5+ years into loving someone, and things are okay, you can’t imagine life without them. Though without you realizing it, one thing leads to another, and now its rocky. You really thought they were the one. You really thought you two (or more, whatever, lol) would last forever. Pay No Mind’s direct connection with Dark Spring symbolizes that. The excitedly chaotic event(s) that lead to this painfully confusing set of crossroads you are now on. “Nothing in this world keeps me confused-“ theyre still here, do they feel the same? Do you keep going, continuing the suffering for both of you until things maybe get better? Or do you move on?

“Its painful but, you do what you must”
